_comment: Attribution register — INPUT to scripts/attribution_check.py, not prose.
What this guards. GitHub resolves a commit's author email against the accounts that have
verified that address, and the Contributors graph caches the result. An address therefore
carries reputation: whoever can verify it can appear as the author of the commits written
under it. Addresses in this repository's history sit on domains the project no longer
bare address on such a domain is a claim waiting for whoever registers the domain next.
The rule that follows: a new commit is accepted only from a noreply address, which GitHub
issues per account and cannot be taken by anyone else. The numeric prefix is the account id,
so the register names GitHub identities rather than mailboxes — no personal address is
History is out of scope. The commits already written keep their addresses; the standing
decision keeps this history as the lab notebook and publishes a clean-room snapshot later,
so this file gates new commits only.
